role_agent_name: Maritime safety and vessel registry lead (MSVR)
abstract: Maintains vessel statutory seaworthiness certifications and certified per-vessel passenger capacity ratings
system_message:
You are the Maritime safety and vessel registry lead (MSVR). Your business responsibilities include maintaining vessel statutory seaworthiness certifications and certified per-vessel passenger capacity ratings, as well as recording drydock hull ultrasonic thickness testing.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains vessel statutory seaworthiness certifications and certified per-vessel passenger capacity ratings（SEAW）
information_points.content:
MSVR-SEAW-GBO：For the Hydrofoil-assisted rapid response consortium, the vessels assigned to the candidate evacuation fleet do not possess valid vessel seaworthiness certification, while the certified vessel passenger capacity stands at 120 person/vessel.
MSVR-SEAW-XEK：For the High-speed wave-piercing catamaran fleet, all vessels assigned to the candidate evacuation fleet hold valid vessel seaworthiness certification, and the certified vessel passenger capacity is 120 person/vessel according to the vessel passenger safety license.
MSVR-SEAW-6EF：For the Deep-draft Ro-Pax ferry contingency charter, all vessels assigned to the candidate evacuation fleet hold valid vessel seaworthiness certification, and each vessel possesses a certified vessel passenger capacity of 180 person/vessel under its emergency passenger safety license.

information_points.title: Drydock hull ultrasonic thickness testing（HULL）
information_points.content:
MSVR-HULL-VGN：For the Hydrofoil-assisted rapid response consortium, the lowest measured minimum plate residual thickness during the annual drydock hull audit is 16.2 mm across critical structural bottom plates.
MSVR-HULL-M1N：During the annual drydock ultrasonic hull gauging survey for the Deep-draft Ro-Pax ferry contingency charter, the candidate bottom plates recorded a minimum plate residual thickness of 12.5 mm across critical structural frames.
MSVR-HULL-14L：During the annual drydock ultrasonic hull gauging survey for the High-speed wave-piercing catamaran fleet, the minimum plate residual thickness measured across bottom plates at critical structural frames is 14.0 mm.
